title: Member Removed From A Privileged Group Outside Governance Automation
detection_hypothesis: If group membership is manipulated to cover tracks or to remove defenders, the removal event will be raised by an interactive administrator rather than by the governance automation account.

field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.TargetUserName: Account or group that was the object of the audited action.
field_semantics.SubjectUserName: Account that performed the audited action.

collection_prerequisites: The relevant advanced audit policy subcategory is enabled for success events.
Domain controller Security logs are forwarded for directory-scoped events.
expected_collection_gaps: Events raised on a domain controller that is not forwarding logs are invisible.
Security log wrapping on busy controllers can drop events before forwarding.
normalization_assumptions: EventID is an integer and Channel is the literal string Security.
Account names are provided without the domain prefix in TargetUserName.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines rename EventID to event.code or similar.
Directory attribute events may arrive with XML-encoded values.
retention_considerations: Security log volume varies widely; 180 to 365 days is common for identity events.
false_positive_strategy: Benign removals cluster around recertification campaigns and are performed by reviewers. Tune by correlating with the campaign window rather than by excluding individual administrators.
tuning_guidance: Keep the governance service filter narrow and named. Avoid excluding human administrator accounts, since those are the accounts most likely to be abused.
test_strategy: Positive cases remove members from a domain group and from the local administrators group. Negative cases cover the governance service, a non-privileged group, and an addition event.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
